headline: The three disputes and their provisional-credit flags follow cleanly from the docs, but the gold's expedited shipping relies on the simulated customer accepting an offer the script never mentions.

issues.summary: Gold[4] orders the replacement with expedited_shipping=true. Unlike tasks 036/037, this user script has no 'if offered expedited shipping, accept it' line, and expedited costs $10 on a Silver card. The doc tells the agent to ask and to strongly recommend expedited for fraud, so acceptance is the natural simulator reply, but it isn't scripted.
evidence: task_036/037 user_scenario step 6: "If offered expedited shipping, accept it" (absent in task_038)

doc_credit_cards_credit_card_replacements_001: "Ask whether they want expedited shipping (advise on possible fees by tier...)" and "If the reason is fraud_suspected or stolen, strongly recommend expedited shipping"
issues.why_it_matters: If the simulator declines the $10 fee, or the agent doesn't ask and the tool default (False) applies, the order record differs and the DB hash fails, even though the agent followed procedure.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the 'If offered expedited shipping, accept it' line to the user scenario, as in tasks 036/037.

solution_check: Amazon on Silver: 10/05 $89.99 (txn_e45e7acb56a0) fraud, no merchant contact, so eligible. 10/08 $124.50 (txn_28cb62125078): wrong item received, so goods_services_not_as_described with contacted=true, NOT eligible by reason. 10/10 $89.99 (txn_2017c3b2b119): duplicate_charge, but the customer didn't contact the merchant, and criterion 5 requires that for non-fraud reasons, so NOT eligible. All are full_refund, cancel_and_reissue, last-4 5320, noticed 11/14/2025. The $42.17 and $67.89 charges are excluded. The replacement goes to the work address, fraud_suspected. This all matches the gold, and the gold replays cleanly.
prior_note: The prior review rated this clean; I add a Minor scripting gap (expedited shipping unscripted). The dispute logic itself is confirmed correct.
notes: The author notes call the duplicate 'eligible', but the gold correctly marks it false under doc_015 criterion 5. The notes aren't agent-visible. 'Sent the wrong item' could be read as goods_services_not_received, which would be eligible (purchase >30 days ago, merchant contacted). doc_014's definition, 'Received item/service differs from description', fits the gold's reason better. Criterion 4 doesn't bind here: the third dispute sees at most 2 prior, which is 'not more than 2'.
